# FDGA037

> DO use “`private protected`” instead of “`protected private`” for a member that can be called by derived types within the same assembly.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section A.1.5 Member Modifiers.

This is a coding style convention. The book treats the appendix A conventions as suggestions, so you can override it.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: IDE0036
- Automatic fix: yes
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Language: [C# 7.2+] (before that: Before C# 7.2 there is no 'private protected'; use 'internal' or 'protected'.)
- Status: verified
